facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: On the issuer-adjusted measure, total debt to EBITDA was 6.70x at FY2024, 9.42x at FY2025 and 8.79x at 2026-06-30, and net debt to EBITDA was 6.35x, 7.75x and 8.03x. Debt rose faster than earnings because Queen joined the group in February 2025 and the debt of Bally's Intralot was consolidated from October 2025, and the FY2025 ratio sets year-end debt against a Successor period shorter than a year; adding the Predecessor period's adjusted EBITDA lowers FY2025 total leverage to 8.96x. On reported EBITDA the ratios are 28.45x at FY2024 and 111.47x at FY2025 and are not calculable at 2026-06-30 because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is negative, so the leverage assessment rests on the issuer's add-backs, none of which is stated as realised or unrealised. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The consolidated figures combine two obligor groups that are insulated from each other: Bally's Intralot does not guarantee Bally's Corporation's debt and a breach under the Bally's Corporation revolver has no implications under Bally's Intralot's debt documents, so the principal debt of Bally's Intralot of USD 2,011,800 thousand and the USD 2,898,268 thousand of revolver, term loan and note principal at Bally's Corporation sit in separate groups. Splitting last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA by segment, which is analyst judgement and not an issuer measure, Bally's Intralot's segments earn USD 391,035 thousand and carry principal debt of 5.14x that amount, while the Bally's Corporation group earns USD 121,775 thousand after triple-net rent and carries principal debt of 23.80x that amount. The consolidated 8.79x therefore understates the leverage faced by lenders to Bally's Corporation, because it counts Bally's Intralot's earnings, which are shared with its 42.1% minority holders and, as far as the sources show, reach Bally's Corporation only through dividends. Basis: calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is operational: revenue is growing, adjusted EBITDA of USD 512,810 thousand over twelve months is above the FY2025 Successor figure of USD 478,009 thousand, the Twin River sale-leaseback released USD 685,000 thousand of cash, and Bally's Intralot's own principal leverage of 5.14x is moderate. - The Predecessor period from 2025-01-01 to 2025-02-07 is not carried as a period column, so FY2025 income, cash-flow and ratio figures cover only the Successor period and cannot be compared with FY2024 or annualised; severity Medium; action: add a combined period only once the break in accounting basis is accepted, using the Predecessor figures already in the sources. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3 - Reported EBITDA is not stated by the issuer and is derived from net loss, and it is negative over the last twelve months, which restricts every leverage and cover ratio on a reported basis at 2026-06-30; severity High; action: obtain the covenant EBITDA definition and any unadjusted EBITDA given to lenders. Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107 - The issuer does not state whether any add-back in adjusted EBITDA is realised or unrealised, which restricts how much of the adjusted figure can be relied on; severity Medium; action: obtain add-back detail from the compliance certificates. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80 - Letters of credit under the Bally's Corporation revolver are not stated, and the gap between commitments less borrowings and the stated availability is unexplained, so the undrawn figure is limited to the amount the filing states; severity Medium; action: obtain the compliance certificate. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C22 - The split of consolidated cash between Bally's Corporation's own group and Bally's Intralot is not stated, which restricts net leverage and liquidity for the Bally's Corporation group; severity High; action: obtain stand-alone Bally's Intralot balance sheets. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11 - The terms of the fifth amendment to the credit agreement dated 2026-07-29, the Bronx loan term sheet, the equity letter of intent and the evoke offer are not stated, which restricts any estimate of net debt after 2026-06-30; severity High; action: obtain the current reports and offer documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3 - No document is dated after 2026-08-14, so the October 2026 revolver step-down and any later draw, repayment or financing are not observable; severity High; action: supply filings dated 2026-08-15 to 2026-11-05. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 75; Source readiness (CP-0) - The waived covenant is described inconsistently across the two latest quarterly reports, and the covenant levels and the minimum liquidity requirement are not printed, which restricts any statement of covenant headroom; severity High; action: obtain the executed credit agreement and waiver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-Q_2026-03-31_baly-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 43 - Lines that the filings print as a dash are shown as not supplied rather than zero, and lines that an interim statement folds into other items are shown as not supplied for those columns, which restricts line-by-line comparison between annual and interim statements only; severity Low; action: confirm nil values against the filing notes where a line-level comparison is needed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6 - Statements of financial position at 2025-06-30, 2025-09-30 and 2026-03-31 are not carried as columns, and the September 2025 and March 2026 quarterly reports served only as cross-checks, which restricts quarterly trend analysis; severity Low; action: add those columns on request. Basis: 10-Q_2025-09-30_baly-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-03-31_baly-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2 - Revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not stated, which limits the FY2024 liquidity row to cash; severity Low; action: obtain the 2024 annual report. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162 - The revolver margin, the revolver balance maturing in October 2026, the scheduled amortisation of the term loans, the terms and security of the Bally's Intralot revolver and supplemental indenture, and the reference rate of the Bally's Intralot revolver are not stated, and the carrying values of the foreign-currency instruments are printed in US dollars only, which restricts the debt instrument register; severity Low; action: obtain the credit agreements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37 - The debt of Bally's Intralot is not ranked against the debt of Bally's Corporation in the debt stack because no source states a legal rank across the two obligor groups, which restricts cumulative leverage to the Bally's Corporation facilities; severity Medium; action: obtain the structure and intercreditor documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36 - The segment-based split of adjusted EBITDA between the two obligor groups is analyst judgement, and unallocated corporate costs follow the issuer's segment allocation, which restricts the Bally's Corporation group leverage to an estimate; severity Medium; action: obtain restricted-group financial statements. Basis: calculation C25; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188 - The cash-flow classification of the development advances received from GLPI for the Chicago project is not stated, which restricts the reading of free cash flow; severity Medium; action: confirm in the notes to the cash-flow statement. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 70 - Operating measures such as rated visitation and online player counts are quoted only as isolated growth rates, so no comparable series exists; severity Low; action: obtain an operating metrics supplement. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4 - Income taxes paid are not printed for the Predecessor year, which restricts cash-tax comparison with FY2025; severity Low; action: obtain the 2024 annual report tax note. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183 - Last-twelve-month revenue and adjusted EBITDA are not shown in the annual-period chart table because the half-year balance-sheet date does not match an annual duration; severity Low; action: read them from the constructed-period register. Basis: calculation C06 - Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed at FY2024 and FY2025, so debt by seniority is shown only at 2026-06-30; severity Low; action: obtain the debt notes with instrument-level carrying values. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162 - The carrying values of the two revolving facilities are not printed and are taken as equal to principal because the residual of total debt less the other nine carrying values equals their principal exactly; severity Low; action: confirm from the debt note. Basis: calculation C31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13 - The undrawn amount of the Bally's Intralot revolver is denominated in euro and is excluded from undrawn committed facilities because no rate is stated and it sits in a separate obligor group; severity Low; action: obtain the euro-dollar rate used by the issuer if a consolidated figure is wanted. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: One holder controls every creditor-relevant decision, so the board is not an independent check. Standard General beneficially owned 67.1% of the common stock at 2026-02-28, down from 73.8% at the February 2025 merger, the company is a controlled company exempt from independent-board requirements, and Standard General's managing partner is Executive Chairman. Financing, acquisition and distribution decisions therefore reach creditors without a minority check, which makes the legal documents and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement, which restricts distributions and new debt above a leverage of 5.50x on its own definition, the real constraints. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Overall, the evidence supports a medium sponsor and governance risk level. The supported behaviour is a controlling holder presiding over an acquisitive and development-heavy strategy that rests on landlord funding and lender waivers, which matters because it leaves creditors without equity support or board checks and implies refinancing and liquidity risk rather than leakage risk. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends or documented fee extraction and the willingness of lenders to waive; further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit and lease documents, and any sponsor equity commitment. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that nothing in the sources shows value leaving the group: no dividend, no related-party fee and no priming transaction appear, Standard General's reported holding is lower at 67.1% than the 73.8% at the merger closing, lenders granted a conditional waiver and amendments instead of enforcing, and GLPI is advancing Chicago construction costs. A binding Bronx loan with third-party equity, a sponsor equity cure or a disclosed absence of fees would move the view toward low risk; a distribution, a related-party transaction funded with debt, a further waiver without deleveraging or an uptier or priming step would move it to high. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Refinancing capacity is weaker for the unsecured notes than for the secured loans, and the real wall is 2029. The disclosed fair value of the 2029 notes is 69.64% of principal and of the 2031 notes 63.00%, against 99.14% for the 2026 term loans, and the term loans mature on 2029-03-01 if the 2029 notes remain outstanding, so USD 1,859,518 thousand, or 37.87% of principal, falls on one refinancing date; 29.14% of principal falls due by the end of 2029. The unsecured notes can only be refinanced on better terms if earnings recover or an equity investor joins, which is why the Bronx financing outcome matters beyond the Bronx. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Bally's presents a not fully assessable business profile supported by scale, diversification and asset value, but credit quality is constrained by liquidity, negative free cash flow and fixed landlord claims. Cash-flow durability appears weak because capital spending and cash interest together exceed adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Bronx financing, a revolver extension and the pricing of the 2029 refinancing. ## Findings
### Bottom line

Bally's Corporation's seven supplied documents support a credit snapshot as of 2026-11-05, but only with stated limits: the newest document is 83 days old, so creditors should treat liquidity, covenant and going-concern conclusions as dated to the second quarter of 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 75; calculation C01

The June 2026 quarterly report is the first supplied document to state substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern. Lenders conditionally waived the leverage covenant in May 2026, and revolver availability is scheduled to fall in October 2026 as part of the facility matures. No credit agreement, indenture, amendment dated July 29, 2026, credit rating or market quote is supplied, and nothing covers the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

The audited 2025 statements carry an unqualified opinion, but the opinion on internal control is adverse because of a tax-review weakness, and the acquired businesses were outside that assessment. The preliminary 2025 release and the annual report agree on the revenue, segment earnings, cash and debt lines compared.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 193; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 194; EX-99.1_2026-03-16_ex991q42025earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-03-16_ex991q42025earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162

## Findings
### Bottom line

Bally's Corporation's debt is not covered by its reported earnings: at 2026-06-30 net debt is 8.03x issuer-adjusted last-twelve-month EBITDA, and reported EBITDA is negative over the same twelve months, so repayment depends on asset sales, new financing and the lenders' conditional covenant waiver.
Basis: calculation C16; calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38

The issuer's adjusted measure is stated after triple-net rent and, in the 2026 half-year, adds back fair-value losses and other non-operating items while removing a sale-leaseback gain, so it is the usable denominator; on it, total debt is 8.79x and cash interest cover is 1.15x. The latest quarterly report states substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern, and the statements carry no adjustment for it. The FY2025 column covers only the Successor period from 2025-02-08, so year-on-year comparisons are not like-for-like.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107
### Key findings

On the issuer-adjusted measure, total debt to EBITDA was 6.70x at FY2024, 9.42x at FY2025 and 8.79x at 2026-06-30, and net debt to EBITDA was 6.35x, 7.75x and 8.03x. Debt rose faster than earnings because Queen joined the group in February 2025 and the debt of Bally's Intralot was consolidated from October 2025, and the FY2025 ratio sets year-end debt against a Successor period shorter than a year; adding the Predecessor period's adjusted EBITDA lowers FY2025 total leverage to 8.96x. On reported EBITDA the ratios are 28.45x at FY2024 and 111.47x at FY2025 and are not calculable at 2026-06-30 because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is negative, so the leverage assessment rests on the issuer's add-backs, none of which is stated as realised or unrealised.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C18; calculation C21; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61

In the six months to 2026-06-30 the issuer reaches adjusted EBITDA of USD 247,318 thousand from reported EBITDA of USD 76,346 thousand through net add-backs of USD 170,972 thousand, led by USD 186,005 thousand of non-operating items that include fair-value and debt-extinguishment losses and partly offset by the removal of a USD 105,845 thousand sale-leaseback gain. Transaction costs of USD 28,568 thousand and development costs of USD 33,264 thousand in the half-year are added back in every period shown, so creditors should treat adjusted EBITDA as a ceiling on recurring earnings rather than a settled figure.
Basis: calculation C37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60–61; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80

Cash interest cover on adjusted EBITDA fell from 1.58x at FY2024 to 1.40x at FY2025 and 1.15x at 2026-06-30, and on reported EBITDA it is 0.37x, 0.12x and -0.10x. Last-twelve-month cash interest of USD 444,640 thousand now absorbs most of adjusted EBITDA of USD 512,810 thousand, and the 2026 term loans carry a margin of 750 bp over term SOFR with a floor of 300 bp, so a modest fall in earnings leaves little room above break-even cover.
Basis: calculation C17; calculation C20; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34

Operating cash flow was USD -11,014 thousand in the FY2025 Successor period and USD -265,936 thousand in the first half of 2026, so free cash flow after capital expenditure and capitalised software is USD -532,312 thousand over the last twelve months. The 2026 half-year includes up-front licence payments of USD -98,906 thousand and a working-capital change of USD -159,699 thousand, and it excludes an acquisition of gaming licences of USD -502,000 thousand, so the group is funding development and licences from asset sales and borrowing: the half-year took in USD 685,000 thousand of sale-leaseback proceeds and repaid a net USD 49,087 thousand of debt.
Basis: calculation C33; calculation C39; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 109–110; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

Reported liquidity is thin and shrinking. Cash was USD 390,184 thousand at 2026-06-30 against USD 798,423 thousand at FY2025, and the revolver had USD 195.8 million available against USD 588.1 million. The filing says total revolver availability will fall to about USD 319 million from October 2026; read as the commitment limit, and with USD 303,750 thousand drawn, it would leave about USD 15.25 million undrawn if the drawn balance were unchanged and no letters of credit were outstanding. The as-of date falls after that step-down and no supplied document shows the position since. Restricted cash of USD 97,587 thousand, which includes player deposits, is excluded throughout, and the sources do not split consolidated cash between Bally's Corporation's own group and Bally's Intralot.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64

The consolidated figures combine two obligor groups that are insulated from each other: Bally's Intralot does not guarantee Bally's Corporation's debt and a breach under the Bally's Corporation revolver has no implications under Bally's Intralot's debt documents, so the principal debt of Bally's Intralot of USD 2,011,800 thousand and the USD 2,898,268 thousand of revolver, term loan and note principal at Bally's Corporation sit in separate groups. Splitting last-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA by segment, which is analyst judgement and not an issuer measure, Bally's Intralot's segments earn USD 391,035 thousand and carry principal debt of 5.14x that amount, while the Bally's Corporation group earns USD 121,775 thousand after triple-net rent and carries principal debt of 23.80x that amount. The consolidated 8.79x therefore understates the leverage faced by lenders to Bally's Corporation, because it counts Bally's Intralot's earnings, which are shared with its 42.1% minority holders and, as far as the sources show, reach Bally's Corporation only through dividends.
Basis: calculation C24; calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11

Carrying value of debt is USD 403,368 thousand, or 8.22%, below contractual principal because fair-value adjustments of USD -351,399 thousand and unamortised discount of USD -51,969 thousand are netted, so leverage measured on principal would be higher than every ratio quoted here. Operating lease liabilities of USD 2,392,267 thousand sit outside debt; adding them to debt and measuring against adjusted EBITDAR gives 9.54x, an analyst judgement because EBITDAR adds back only triple-net rent. At the 2025 year-end a New York gaming licence fee of USD 500,000 thousand and contingent consideration of USD 115,000 thousand, together USD 615,000 thousand, sat in accrued liabilities outside debt and were paid in the first quarter of 2026, and deferred payable arrangements of USD 27.7 million at 2026-06-30, against USD 47.0 million at 2025-12-31, are also carried outside debt.

Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C35; calculation C30; calculation C40; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162

In the quarter to 2026-06-30 revenue rose 20.49% to USD 792,234 thousand while adjusted EBITDA changed by -4.03% to USD 124,034 thousand, the first quarter to carry the UK gaming tax increase. In May 2026 lenders conditionally waived the net leverage covenant, subject to a minimum liquidity requirement whose level is not stated; a fifth amendment to the credit agreement is dated 2026-07-29 and its terms are not described; in July the company signed a non-binding term sheet for a Bronx loan and in August a letter of intent with a potential equity investor, neither with an amount stated; and on 2026-07-27 Bally's Intralot signed GBP 261.8 million of new facilities and paid a dividend of which USD 13.9 million went to minority holders, lifting pro forma net debt to USD 4,130,416 thousand.

Basis: calculation C34; calculation C31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 74; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is operational: revenue is growing, adjusted EBITDA of USD 512,810 thousand over twelve months is above the FY2025 Successor figure of USD 478,009 thousand, the Twin River sale-leaseback released USD 685,000 thousand of cash, and Bally's Intralot's own principal leverage of 5.14x is moderate. A binding Bronx loan or equity sale that extends liquidity beyond the October 2026 step-down, filings after 2026-06-30 showing liquidity above the waiver minimum, or positive last-twelve-month reported EBITDA would each move this view toward manageable leverage; a further fall in quarterly adjusted EBITDA, a revolver drawn close to its reduced commitments, or an adverse change in the waiver would move it the other way.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C26; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33
### Limitations

These statements are consolidated and mix a Predecessor and a Successor basis, so FY2024 and FY2025 are not comparable and the short Predecessor period from 2025-01-01 to 2025-02-07 sits outside every column. Reported EBITDA is derived from net loss because the issuer states only an adjusted measure, and no covenant EBITDA, covenant level or minimum liquidity amount is supplied, so no covenant headroom is stated. The latest balance sheet is 128 days before the as-of date, the newest document is 83 days old, and the interim statements are unaudited.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C41; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2

## Gaps

- The Predecessor period from 2025-01-01 to 2025-02-07 is not carried as a period column, so FY2025 income, cash-flow and ratio figures cover only the Successor period and cannot be compared with FY2024 or annualised; severity Medium; action: add a combined period only once the break in accounting basis is accepted, using the Predecessor figures already in the sources.

- Reported EBITDA is not stated by the issuer and is derived from net loss, and it is negative over the last twelve months, which restricts every leverage and cover ratio on a reported basis at 2026-06-30; severity High; action: obtain the covenant EBITDA definition and any unadjusted EBITDA given to lenders.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107

- The issuer does not state whether any add-back in adjusted EBITDA is realised or unrealised, which restricts how much of the adjusted figure can be relied on; severity Medium; action: obtain add-back detail from the compliance certificates.

- Letters of credit under the Bally's Corporation revolver are not stated, and the gap between commitments less borrowings and the stated availability is unexplained, so the undrawn figure is limited to the amount the filing states; severity Medium; action: obtain the compliance certificate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C22

- The split of consolidated cash between Bally's Corporation's own group and Bally's Intralot is not stated, which restricts net leverage and liquidity for the Bally's Corporation group; severity High; action: obtain stand-alone Bally's Intralot balance sheets.

- The terms of the fifth amendment to the credit agreement dated 2026-07-29, the Bronx loan term sheet, the equity letter of intent and the evoke offer are not stated, which restricts any estimate of net debt after 2026-06-30; severity High; action: obtain the current reports and offer documents.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 74; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

- No document is dated after 2026-08-14, so the October 2026 revolver step-down and any later draw, repayment or financing are not observable; severity High; action: supply filings dated 2026-08-15 to 2026-11-05.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 75; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The waived covenant is described inconsistently across the two latest quarterly reports, and the covenant levels and the minimum liquidity requirement are not printed, which restricts any statement of covenant headroom; severity High; action: obtain the executed credit agreement and waiver.

- Lines that the filings print as a dash are shown as not supplied rather than zero, and lines that an interim statement folds into other items are shown as not supplied for those columns, which restricts line-by-line comparison between annual and interim statements only; severity Low; action: confirm nil values against the filing notes where a line-level comparison is needed.

- Statements of financial position at 2025-06-30, 2025-09-30 and 2026-03-31 are not carried as columns, and the September 2025 and March 2026 quarterly reports served only as cross-checks, which restricts quarterly trend analysis; severity Low; action: add those columns on request.
- Revolver availability at 2024-12-31 is not stated, which limits the FY2024 liquidity row to cash; severity Low; action: obtain the 2024 annual report.

- The revolver margin, the revolver balance maturing in October 2026, the scheduled amortisation of the term loans, the terms and security of the Bally's Intralot revolver and supplemental indenture, and the reference rate of the Bally's Intralot revolver are not stated, and the carrying values of the foreign-currency instruments are printed in US dollars only, which restricts the debt instrument register; severity Low; action: obtain the credit agreements.

- The debt of Bally's Intralot is not ranked against the debt of Bally's Corporation in the debt stack because no source states a legal rank across the two obligor groups, which restricts cumulative leverage to the Bally's Corporation facilities; severity Medium; action: obtain the structure and intercreditor documents.

- The segment-based split of adjusted EBITDA between the two obligor groups is analyst judgement, and unallocated corporate costs follow the issuer's segment allocation, which restricts the Bally's Corporation group leverage to an estimate; severity Medium; action: obtain restricted-group financial statements.
Basis: calculation C25; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188

- The cash-flow classification of the development advances received from GLPI for the Chicago project is not stated, which restricts the reading of free cash flow; severity Medium; action: confirm in the notes to the cash-flow statement.

- Operating measures such as rated visitation and online player counts are quoted only as isolated growth rates, so no comparable series exists; severity Low; action: obtain an operating metrics supplement.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4
- Income taxes paid are not printed for the Predecessor year, which restricts cash-tax comparison with FY2025; severity Low; action: obtain the 2024 annual report tax note.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183

- Last-twelve-month revenue and adjusted EBITDA are not shown in the annual-period chart table because the half-year balance-sheet date does not match an annual duration; severity Low; action: read them from the constructed-period register.
Basis: calculation C06

- Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed at FY2024 and FY2025, so debt by seniority is shown only at 2026-06-30; severity Low; action: obtain the debt notes with instrument-level carrying values.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162

- The carrying values of the two revolving facilities are not printed and are taken as equal to principal because the residual of total debt less the other nine carrying values equals their principal exactly; severity Low; action: confirm from the debt note.
Basis: calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31

- Pro forma net leverage after the Bally's Intralot dividend and the new facilities cannot be stated because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is negative and the new facility draw-down is not stated; severity Medium; action: restate once reported EBITDA is positive or a covenant EBITDA is supplied.
Basis: calculation C31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13

- The undrawn amount of the Bally's Intralot revolver is denominated in euro and is excluded from undrawn committed facilities because no rate is stated and it sits in a separate obligor group; severity Low; action: obtain the euro-dollar rate used by the issuer if a consolidated figure is wanted.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors are exposed to a controlled company whose growth programme has outrun its funded liquidity: no dividends or fee leakage are documented, but no sponsor equity support is either, so sponsor and governance risk is medium and protection rests on documents, not alignment.

Half of revenue comes from casinos, most of them leased from one landlord, and 41.14% from Bally's Intralot, a separate obligor group; Chicago, Bronx and Las Vegas commitments, and a controlling holder whose managing partner chairs the board, mean creditor protection rests on the executed documents and lender waivers, not on board independence.
Basis: calculation A02; calculation A03; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45
### Key findings

One holder controls every creditor-relevant decision, so the board is not an independent check. Standard General beneficially owned 67.1% of the common stock at 2026-02-28, down from 73.8% at the February 2025 merger, the company is a controlled company exempt from independent-board requirements, and Standard General's managing partner is Executive Chairman. Financing, acquisition and distribution decisions therefore reach creditors without a minority check, which makes the legal documents and the Rhode Island regulatory agreement, which restricts distributions and new debt above a leverage of 5.50x on its own definition, the real constraints.

The 2025 deals changed what creditors own: Casinos & Resorts fell from 56.75% of Successor-period revenue in FY2025 to 50.44% in the first half of 2026, while Bally's Intralot rose from 34.90% to 41.14%. Bally's Intralot brings lottery contracts and interactive operations in a subsidiary with its own lenders and minority holders, so part of group revenue growth sits behind other claims, and the UK tax increase hit its consumer segment in the second quarter of 2026.
Basis: calculation A01; calculation A02; calculation A03; calculation A12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

Landlord claims sit ahead of lenders in practice and are growing. Triple-net rent takes 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR over the last twelve months, the Twin River sale-leaseback added USD 56.0 million of annual rent in February 2026, and the Chicago ground lease adds 8.5% of every GLPI development advance to rent. After any refinancing, extension or majority amendment of the credit agreement the Chicago ground lease cross-defaults to the two GLPI master leases, so a default under the master leases would then also put the Chicago site and its landlord-funded construction at risk.

Basis: calculation A06; calculation A11; calculation A09; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 39

The development programme is the main discretionary claim on cash and is only partly funded. Chicago must spend at least USD 1,340.0 million under its host community agreement with about USD 400.0 million remaining and an expected overrun that the filing cannot yet estimate, GLPI advances of up to USD 940.0 million are conditional on the company showing unrestricted access to funds, and the USD 4.0 billion Bronx project has only a non-binding term sheet and a letter of intent behind it after a USD 500.0 million licence fee and USD 115 million of contingent consideration were paid in the first quarter of 2026. If the Bronx financing is not completed, the remaining project obligations would fall on the same liquidity that supports the revolver.

Basis: calculation A09; calculation A10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 72; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49

Sponsor and company behaviour in the sources is mixed rather than extractive. No cash dividend was paid in either period and the filings state no intention to pay one, and no management or monitoring fee to Standard General appears in the documents read; against that, the company paid USD 416,180 thousand of cash to non-rolling shareholders at USD 18.25 a share in the first quarter of 2025, bought more Bally's Intralot shares for USD 24,359 thousand in the first half of 2026 while liquidity was falling, and entered a total return swap on Bally's Intralot shares of up to EUR 50.0 million in June 2026 ahead of the evoke offer.

Disclosure quality limits how well creditors can monitor the group. A material weakness over income-tax review remains open at the June 2026 report, disclosure controls were not effective in both the annual and the June report, the annual report was filed under an extension, and the June quarterly report omits market-risk disclosure; the 2026 proxy statement that would carry board composition and compensation is not in the sources.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 193; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 73; EX-99.1_2026-03-16_ex991q42025earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 197

Overall, the evidence supports a medium sponsor and governance risk level. The supported behaviour is a controlling holder presiding over an acquisitive and development-heavy strategy that rests on landlord funding and lender waivers, which matters because it leaves creditors without equity support or board checks and implies refinancing and liquidity risk rather than leakage risk. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends or documented fee extraction and the willingness of lenders to waive; further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit and lease documents, and any sponsor equity commitment.
Basis: calculation A04; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that nothing in the sources shows value leaving the group: no dividend, no related-party fee and no priming transaction appear, Standard General's reported holding is lower at 67.1% than the 73.8% at the merger closing, lenders granted a conditional waiver and amendments instead of enforcing, and GLPI is advancing Chicago construction costs. A binding Bronx loan with third-party equity, a sponsor equity cure or a disclosed absence of fees would move the view toward low risk; a distribution, a related-party transaction funded with debt, a further waiver without deleveraging or an uptier or priming step would move it to high.
### Limitations

- Standard General's 67.1% holding is dated 2026-02-28 and no later holding is supplied, so the control finding would change only if the holding fell below a majority of votes, which no document indicates.

- No sponsor fund vintage, remaining fund life, management or monitoring fee, or equity-contribution amount is stated, so the medium risk level could rise if fees or exit pressure were disclosed and cannot fall to low without a documented equity commitment.

- Segment definitions were re-cut in the fourth quarter of 2025 and prior periods recast, so the shift in revenue mix between casinos and Bally's Intralot depends on the recast boundaries and is directional only.

- Only issuer-level conduct is assessed, so the development-risk finding for Chicago, the Bronx and Las Vegas rests on disclosed commitments and costs rather than delivery evidence, and would change if budget or milestone documents were supplied.

- The ownership map covers the entities the filings name; intermediate holding companies and any parent support of Bally's Intralot obligations are not described, so the finding that the two obligor groups are separate holds only for the documents read.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The 2025 merger of Bally's Corporation with Standard General's Queen Casino & Entertainment closed on 2025-02-07: Standard General contributed its Queen shares in exchange for new Bally's common stock, public holders not electing to roll received USD 18.25 in cash per share, and Standard General's group ended with 73.8% of the common stock. The Queen merger was accounted for as a transaction between entities under common control, and the company settled Queen's pre-existing debt and issued USD 500.0 million of 11% first-lien notes due 2028 at closing, which it repaid in full on 2025-10-08.

On 2025-10-08 the company closed the Bally's Intralot transaction: Bally's Intralot paid USD 1.8 billion of cash and issued new shares for Bally's International Interactive, lifting the company's stake to a controlling 57.9% and creating a 42.1% non-controlling interest, and the company assumed Bally's Intralot debt of USD 1.97 billion at a fair value of USD 1.98 billion. New debt in this group since then comprises EUR 600 million of 6.75% senior secured notes and EUR 300 million of floating-rate notes due 2031, a GBP 400.0 million term loan, a euro term loan and a euro revolver, and on 2026-07-27 Bally's Intralot signed a further GBP 261.8 million of senior secured term facilities.

At Bally's Corporation the new debt is the USD 1.1 billion of 2026 term loans signed on 2026-02-11, priced at 750 bp over term SOFR with a 300 bp floor and up to 3.50% payable in kind, which repaid the previous term loan and mature in 2031 unless the 2029 notes remain outstanding on 2029-03-01. The Twin River sale-leaseback to GLPI closed the same day for USD 700.0 million, and the credit agreement amendments of January and May 2026 split the revolver's maturities and raised its margins, while a further amendment dated 2026-07-29 is not described.

Other transactions are the A$200 million investment in The Star from April 2025, now a 37.7% equity stake carried at fair value, the New York licence and land conveyance, and the June 2026 binding offer by Bally's Intralot for evoke plc, whose consideration is not stated in the sources and whose financing is therefore not established.

spans.text: ## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Bally's Corp (baly), as of 2026-11-05, under the credit_snapshot pathway. It combines the business, financial and governance findings of the earlier modules with the seven supplied filings and releases into one credit view, drivers, monitoring triggers and a downside path. Run settings are not issuer evidence and are not listed as a source.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

The fundamental credit profile is weak and liquidity-driven: adjusted EBITDA of USD 512,810 thousand covers cash interest only 1.15x, free cash flow is deeply negative, and going-concern doubt means creditors depend on asset monetisation and refinancing rather than internally generated cash.
Basis: calculation B01; calculation B04; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11

Scale across casinos, online gaming and lottery, a proven ability to sell property for cash and lenders' willingness to waive support the credit; the October 2026 revolver step-down, an unfunded development programme and net debt of USD 4,116,516 thousand, or USD 4,130,416 thousand pro forma for the Bally's Intralot dividend paid on 2026-07-27 with pro forma net leverage not established, weaken it.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B06; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Key findings

Liquidity is the binding weakness and it is shrinking on a known date. Cash was USD 390,184 thousand and the revolver had USD 195.8 million available at 2026-06-30, together USD 585,984 thousand, and the filing says total revolver availability falls to about USD 319 million from October 2026, which would leave about USD 15.25 million undrawn if read as the commitment limit with the drawn balance unchanged. The company states that without its planned financings it does not project meeting the minimum liquidity requirement of the waiver or the reinstated leverage covenant, so a revolver whose access depends on a test creditors cannot see is the first thing that breaks; pro forma cash after the 2026-07-27 dividend is not established.

Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Operations do not fund the business, so every obligation is met from asset sales or borrowing. After cash interest, capital expenditure and capitalised software, adjusted EBITDA leaves USD -128,393 thousand, free cash flow over the last twelve months is USD -532,312 thousand, and capital spending absorbs 38.33% of adjusted EBITDA before rent timing, working capital or licence payments. In the first half of 2026 the group received USD 685,000 thousand from the Twin River sale-leaseback and repaid a net USD 49,087 thousand of debt, which shows that deleveraging so far comes from monetising property into fixed rent rather than from earnings.
Basis: calculation B03; calculation B04; calculation B05; calculation B15; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Leverage is high on any measure and the parent group carries the worse half. Total debt is 8.79x issuer-adjusted EBITDA and net debt 8.03x, with pro forma net leverage not established, and reported EBITDA is negative over the last twelve months, so no reported-basis leverage can be stated; splitting segment earnings, which is analyst judgement, puts the principal debt of Bally's Corporation at 23.80x its share of adjusted EBITDA against 5.14x at Bally's Intralot. Lenders to the parent group therefore rely on property monetisation and parent-level financing rather than on the Intralot earnings that sit in the consolidated ratio.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B10; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Refinancing capacity is weaker for the unsecured notes than for the secured loans, and the real wall is 2029. The disclosed fair value of the 2029 notes is 69.64% of principal and of the 2031 notes 63.00%, against 99.14% for the 2026 term loans, and the term loans mature on 2029-03-01 if the 2029 notes remain outstanding, so USD 1,859,518 thousand, or 37.87% of principal, falls on one refinancing date; 29.14% of principal falls due by the end of 2029. The unsecured notes can only be refinanced on better terms if earnings recover or an equity investor joins, which is why the Bronx financing outcome matters beyond the Bronx.
Basis: calculation B08; calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37

Revenue is durable at the regional casinos but margin is not. Casinos & Resorts revenue rose 2.0% and segment Adjusted EBITDAR 3.4% in the second quarter of 2026 and rated visitation rose 4.3%, yet the adjusted EBITDA margin fell from 20.71% in the first half of 2025 to 15.98% in the first half of 2026 and quarterly adjusted EBITDA changed by -4.03% on revenue growth of 20.49%. Triple-net rent takes 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR and the UK gaming tax increase cost about USD 39 million gross in the quarter with close to 65% offset by management action, so fixed claims and regulation, not demand, set the margin.
Basis: calculation B11; calculation B12; calculation B13; calculation B14; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

Financial policy and governance are average at best: a controlling holder with 67.1% of the common stock has received no dividends and no documented fees, but no sponsor equity support is documented while the company buys more Bally's Intralot shares and pursues the evoke offer. Policy therefore adds growth demands to a business that cannot fund its present commitments, and creditor protection rests on documents and lender waivers rather than on sponsor support.
Basis: calculation B17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28

In a downside, the first break is the October 2026 revolver step-down and the minimum liquidity test, not an operating collapse. If the Bronx loan and equity do not close, development spending and cash interest continue to draw on a smaller revolver and falling cash; a failed liquidity test ends the waiver and reinstates the leverage covenant, which the company already projects it could not meet, and the filings do not state how the term loans and notes cross-default. The observable triggers are revolver availability, cash, waiver status and the Bronx financing, and the analysis does not state a run-out date because no forecast is supplied.

Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; calculation B16; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 66
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak view is that creditors and landlords keep funding the company: lenders conditionally waived the leverage covenant, GLPI is advancing Chicago construction costs, the Twin River sale-leaseback realised USD 700.0 million, Bally's Intralot has signed GBP 261.8 million of new term facilities at 5.14x principal leverage on segment earnings, revenue rose 20.49% in the quarter and casinos are growing slowly but positively. A binding Bronx loan with third-party equity, an extension of the revolver beyond October 2026, an equity sale or a second property monetisation at a similar price would move the view toward average; termination of the waiver, availability near USD 15.25 million, a failure to refinance the 2029 notes or a further fall in quarterly adjusted EBITDA would move it to a distressed view.

Basis: calculation B07; calculation B10; calculation B13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 40
### Limitations

- The downside is described qualitatively with no stress figures and no run-out date, so the weak liquidity conclusion rests on direction and on the known October 2026 step-down, and a quantified forecast could bring the date forward or push it back.

- The outlook for UK online trading and lottery contract wins comes from management statements in the second-quarter release, so a stronger recovery than stated would lift the margin finding and a weaker one would deepen it.

- Casinos are assessed from segment totals because property-level results are not supplied, so a weak property inside a stable segment would not show and the revenue-durability finding could be too favourable.

- The ranking of strengths and weaknesses is analyst judgement among supported drivers, and a documented revolver extension or Bronx financing would reorder the top weaknesses rather than add new ones.

- The parent and Bally's Intralot comparison depends on the issuer's segment boundaries, so an intragroup charge or cost allocation not shown would shift the finding that the parent group carries the weaker credit.
### Analytical appendix — complete canonical registers
The sections, registers and report tables that follow carry the analysis behind the findings above.
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest credit supports are scale and spread of earnings, asset value and a willing lender group. Revenue is USD 2,957,917 thousand over the last twelve months across US casinos, online gaming and lottery, so no single property or product dominates; the Twin River sale-leaseback shows that real estate can be sold for USD 700.0 million, and lenders have waived rather than enforced.
Basis: calculation B13; calculation B17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 38; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The weakest points are liquidity, cash conversion and the unfunded development programme. The revolver is the only undrawn source stated for the parent group and it steps down in October 2026, free cash flow is USD -532,312 thousand, rent absorbs 29.06% of Adjusted EBITDAR, and the Bronx project of USD 4.0 billion has only a non-binding term sheet and a letter of intent. Opportunities that would improve credit quality are a binding Bronx financing, the 2027 Chicago opening and the 2028 Las Vegas stadium, and threats are a failed liquidity test, a further UK tax or regulatory change and a Bally's Intralot acquisition that adds debt.
Basis: calculation B04; calculation B07; calculation B11; calculation B16; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_baly-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11
### Company and ownership in credit terms

Bally's Corporation is a casino, interactive and lottery group whose 2025 acquisitions of Queen and a controlling 57.9% of Bally's Intralot lifted revenue to USD 2,957,917 thousand over twelve months, with casinos at 50.44% and Bally's Intralot at 41.14% of first-half 2026 revenue. Cash-flow visibility is moderate because casino revenue is regional and discretionary while lottery contracts are multi-year, but the group is held by a controlling holder with 67.1% of the common stock and by two separate obligor groups, so visibility at the parent group is lower than the consolidated figures suggest.
Basis: calculation B13; calculation B17; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue durability, margins and cash conversion

Revenue visibility is highest at the regional casinos and at lottery contracts and lowest in UK online gaming, where tax rose from 21% to 40% from 2026-04-01 and about USD 39 million of the quarter's earnings was hit before offsets. Operating leverage is high because rent, interest and development spending are fixed, so a small fall in segment earnings removes the cushion after cash interest; capital spending of 38.33% of adjusted EBITDA is only partly discretionary because Chicago is contractually committed.
Basis: calculation B03; calculation B05; calculation B14; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Competitive and external forces

Competitive rivalry is regional, and management named elevated competition in Atlantic City and East Saint Louis as a pressure in the second quarter; entry and substitution risk from online play is not evidenced beyond the company's own strategy of expanding interactive gaming; buyers in lottery are public bodies under long contracts, which supports visibility but needs up-front investment; and the landlord GLPI is the most powerful supplier because rent is fixed and, after a credit agreement refinancing, the Chicago lease cross-defaults to the master leases. Regulation matters to credit through the UK gaming tax increase and through the Rhode Island regulatory agreement, which caps distributions and new debt above a leverage of 5.50x on its own definition; foreign exchange matters because Bally's Intralot's debt is in sterling and euros.

Basis: calculation B14; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_baly-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 49
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is weak on liquidity, free cash flow and margin stability, average on scale and diversification, and average on financial policy because no value leaves the group but no equity enters it. The trend is negative: adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 15.98% in the first half of 2026 from 20.71% a year earlier, net leverage on adjusted EBITDA is 8.03x with pro forma net leverage not established, and the key missing datapoints are covenant levels, the minimum liquidity requirement and any forecast.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook

Over the next one to two years the Chicago permanent casino targets an early 2027 opening, the Las Vegas ballpark is due before the 2028 season, the revolver steps down in October 2026 and the Bronx financing must close; trading tailwinds are rated visitation, UK online growth and new lottery contracts, headwinds are the UK tax and rent growth. Over three to five years the Bronx project of USD 4.0 billion, due to open by 2030, decides whether the group becomes self-funding or carries a second large unfunded commitment.
Basis: calculation B14; calculation B16; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-14_ex991q22026earningsrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Overall credit view

Overall, Bally's presents a not fully assessable business profile supported by scale, diversification and asset value, but credit quality is constrained by liquidity, negative free cash flow and fixed landlord claims. Cash-flow durability appears weak because capital spending and cash interest together exceed adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Bronx financing, a revolver extension and the pricing of the 2029 refinancing. The primary downside path is a failed liquidity test after the October 2026 step-down. Further analysis would require covenant levels, the minimum liquidity requirement, a forecast and filings after 2026-08-14. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: liquidity.
Basis: calculation B03; calculation B06; calculation B07; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
